sections.title: Identification and habitat
sections.text: The catalogue entry represents Lotus corniculatus, bird's-foot trefoil. This temperate Eurasian perennial is usually 10–30 cm tall and grows in meadows and along roadsides; it is also cultivated as forage.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and pods
sections.text: Each leaf has three leaflets and two leaf-like stipules. The yellow flowers, sometimes orange or reddish, produce cylindrical pods 15–30 mm long that radiate like a bird's foot.

sections.title: Caution
sections.text: The species is used as forage and a Swiss veterinary source classifies it as non-poisonous, but some plants or conditions may produce cyanogenic glycosides. Do not assume it is invariably risk-free.
